items.s: The word ‘Hindu’ as a reference to the people of Hind (India) was first used by:
items.x:
Most books and keys: the Arabs. Strictly: the Persians (Achaemenid inscriptions, 'Hidu') used it first (Britannica 'Hinduism').
Of the options, the Arabs used 'Hind/Hindu' for India and its people (al-Hind); the word itself comes from the Iranian (Persian) form of Sindhu, Hindu, used first in Achaemenid inscriptions – not offered here. The Greeks said 'Indoi/India', the Chinese 'Shendu/Yindu'.

items.s: Who was the father of Dhruva?
items.x: In the Vishnu and Bhagavata Puranas Dhruva is the son of King Uttanapada and Suniti. Karna, Dasharatha and Nahusha are unrelated.

items.s: The earliest reference of Andhradesha in foreign literature was found in the writings of
items.x: Megasthenes' Indica (c. 300 BC) is the earliest foreign reference to the Andhras: it mentions their 30 walled towns (forts) and large army. Fa-Hien, Conti and Marco Polo wrote centuries later.

items.s: In which story of the Aitareya Brahmana does the word 'Andhra' first appear?
items.x: 'Andhra' first appears in the Aitareya Brahmana in connection with the Sunahshepa story, not in the Rig Veda.

items.s: In which text does the word 'Andhra' first appear?
items.x: 'Andhra' first appears in the Aitareya Brahmana, in the Sunahshepa story, not in the Rigveda.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: In which year was the wheel invented?
items.x: The wheel first appears in Mesopotamia around 3500 BC. The later dates offered are far too recent.

Historical place - Well-known for

2. Chandra-ketugarh - Terracotta art

3. Ganeshwar - Copper artifacts
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
items.x: Chandraketugarh (terracotta art) and Ganeshwar (copper artefacts) are correctly matched; Burzahom is a Neolithic site of pit dwellings, not rock-cut shrines. So 2 and 3.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: Which metal did the ancient Indians use first?
items.x: Copper was the first metal used in India (Chalcolithic cultures); iron came only around 1000 BCE.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s: The North Indian Plains (Gangetic plains) show very few signs of prehistoric Stone Age life, even though the region is agriculturally rich. In contrast, South India, including Andhra Pradesh, has revealed numerous prehistoric sites. What are the reasons for this contrast?
o: The earliest human migrations first reached South India and moved northward much later.
The North Indian Plains became suitable for human habitation only after 10,000 BCE.
The Deccan Plateau and regions like Andhra Pradesh had abundant stone resources for making tools.
Prehistoric humans avoided South India due to frequent volcanic eruptions in the Deccan region.
items.x: The Deccan and Andhra hills offered abundant quartzite and other stone for tools, and the rocky terrain preserved sites, whereas the thick alluvium of the Gangetic plains buries early sites; the migration and volcano options are false. Moved to Stone Age cultures.

items.s: Which is the largest site of the Jorwe culture?
items.x: Daimabad is the largest Jorwe site in Maharashtra.

items.s: To which period is the Malwa culture dated?
items.x: Malwa is about 1900–1400 BCE; Ahar 2800–1500, Kayatha 2450–1700, Jorwe 1400–700 BCE.

items.s: To which period is the Jorwe culture dated?
items.x: Jorwe (Maharashtra) is about 1400–700 BCE.

items.s: Which of the following Chalcolithic cultures is the oldest?
items.x: Ahar dates to 2800-1500 BCE, older than Kayatha (2450-1700 BCE), Malwa (1900-1400 BCE) and Jorwe (1400-700 BCE).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s: In Andhra Pradesh, during the Neolithic-Chalcolithic period, which system of disposing of the dead was in practice?
items.x: In the Neolithic-Chalcolithic sites of Andhra (Utnur, Nagarjunakonda) adults were laid in extended burials, often with pots; urns were used for children. Post-cremation and mound burials are not typical. Off-topic for the IVC, moved to prehistoric Andhra.

The following statements contains an assertion followed by a reason. Read the statements carefully and answer from the given below options.
Assertion (A): Utnur site has shown the evidence of animal domestication in Andhra Pradesh during Neolithic period
Reason (R): An evidence of wooden enclosure built many times and burning of cow dung repeatedly has been found.
o: A and R is True and R is the correct explanation of A
A and R is True but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is True and R is False
A is False but R is True
items.x: At Utnur (Mahabubnagar) Allchin found ash mounds formed by repeatedly burning cow dung inside wooden cattle stockades, proving Neolithic cattle-keeping. So both are true and R explains A.

items.s:
The following statements contains an assertion followed by a reason. Read the statements carefully and answer from the given below options.
Assertion (A): The Microliths in South Indian were mostly made of milky quartz during Mesolithic period.
Reason (R): Nagarjunakonda and Renigunta sites in Andhra Pradesh have given evidence of these microliths.
o: A and R is True and R is the correct explanation of A
A and R is True but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is True but R is False
A is False but R is True
items.x:
Printed APPSC key: A and R true, R explains A. Strictly R only names find-spots and does not explain why quartz was used, so 'R is not the correct explanation' is the stricter answer.
Both are true: Mesolithic microliths in South India were mostly of milky quartz, and Nagarjunakonda and Renigunta in AP have yielded them. The printed APPSC key links them as assertion and explanation.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
items.s:
The following statements contain an assertion and a reason. Read the statements carefully and answer from the given options.
Assertion (A): There is no evidence of tools making out of animal bones in upper paleolithic context in Andhra Pradesh.
Reason (R): One of the cave sites in Kurnool has given evidence of 90 percent tools being made out of animal bones.
o: A and R is True and R is the correct explanation of A
A and R is True but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is True but R is False
A is False but R is True
items.x: A is false: the Kurnool caves (Muchchatla Chintamani Gavi, Betamcherla) gave Upper Palaeolithic bone tools, about 90% of the tools there being of bone. So R is true.

items.s: In which district is Patapadu, a Chalcolithic site of Andhra Pradesh, located?
items.x: Patapadu is in Kurnool district.

items.s: Burial and post-burial rites are associated with which culture?
items.x: Burial and post-burial rites belong to Megalithic culture; yajna belongs to the Yajurveda, Purushamedha to the Shatapatha Brahmana and ceremonial chanting to the Samaveda.

items.s: Dholavira is especially notable for which combination of features?
o: Dog burial and a red sandstone torso
Bronze chariot and an ivory scale
Horse bones and a circular mud-brick fort
Water reservoirs and a three-part town
items.x: Dholavira is known for its water reservoirs, ten-sign signboard and three-part town.

items.s: To which site does the Great Bath belong?
items.x: The Great Bath belongs to Mohenjo-daro, not Lothal.

items.s: Dholavira had how many urban divisions?
items.x: Dholavira had three divisions: Citadel, Middle Town and Lower Town.

items.s:
Match the following Harappan civilization towns with their archaeological sources:
List-I:
A. Harappa
B. Mohenjo Daro
C. Lothal
D. Rangapur
List-II: i. The great bath ii. Paddy Husk iii. Port City iv. Granary
items.x: Harappa – granary, Mohenjodaro – Great Bath, Lothal – port city (dockyard), Rangpur – paddy husk: A-iv, B-i, C-iii, D-ii.

items.s:
Match
List I (Ancient site) with
List II (Archaeological finding) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:
List I (Ancient site)
A. Lothal
B. Kalibangan
C. Dholavira
D. Banawali
List II (Archaeological finding)
1. Ploughed field
2. Dockyard
3. Terracotta replica of a plough

Codes:
items.x: Lothal – dockyard, Kalibangan – ploughed field, Dholavira – ten-sign inscription, Banawali – terracotta plough: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

items.s: Which one of the following ancient towns is well-known for its elaborate system of water harvesting and management by building a series of dams and channelizing water into connected reservoirs?
items.x: Dholavira had dams, channels and connected reservoirs fed by two seasonal streams – one of the earliest water-management systems.

items.s: From where was the evidence of rock-cut architecture found, with reference to Harappa civilization?
items.x: Dholavira (Kutch) shows rock-cut architecture – rock-cut reservoirs and dressed-stone structures.

items.s: A ploughed field was discovered at –
items.x: Kalibangan (pre-Harappan level) gave the earliest ploughed field with criss-cross furrows.

items.s: Which of the following is a Harappan port?
items.x: Lothal, with its dockyard, was the Harappan port; Alexandria is Egyptian, Mahasthangarh is in Bangladesh and Nagapattinam is a Chola port.

items.s: During the Indus Valley Civilization, the beads manufacturing industry was located at
items.x: Chanhudaro is the Harappan bead-making centre (Mackay's bead factory, 'Lancashire of India'); Lothal also made beads, but Chanhudaro is the key.

items.s: From which archaeological site of Indus Valley Civilization, the figures or models of boat are found?
items.x: A terracotta boat model came from Lothal and boats are depicted on Mohenjodaro seals.

items.s: In which of the following Harappan cities, furrows of ploughed fields have been found?
items.x: Furrows of a ploughed field were found at Kalibangan (Rajasthan).

items.s:
Match the following.
List I
List II

A. Harappa
1. Cemetry R-37

B. Lothal
2. Dockyard

C. Kalibangan
3. Dancing girl statue

D. Mohenjodaro
4. Furrowed land
Codes A B C D
items.x: Harappa – Cemetery R-37, Lothal – dockyard, Kalibangan – furrowed land, Mohenjodaro – Dancing Girl: 1 2 4 3.

items.s: Surkotada is particularly associated with which archaeological finding?
o: Horse bones, though the identification is disputed
The earliest known gold coin hoard
items.x: Surkotada is a fortified Harappan site in Kutch associated with horse bones; the interpretation is disputed.

items.s: Where were the bronze Dancing Girl, the Priest-King and the Pashupati seal found?
items.x: Mohenjodaro has yielded the bronze Dancing Girl, the Priest-King, the Pashupati seal, the Great Bath, the Great Granary and an assembly hall.

items.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Harappa — two rows of six granaries
items.x: The ten-sign inscription signboard belongs to Dholavira. Harappa is associated with Cemetery H, a red sandstone male torso and two rows of six granaries.

items.s: At which site was a copper dog found?
items.x: Lothal yielded a copper dog, rice husk, a Persian Gulf seal and three double burials.

items.s: Evidence of an earthquake has been found at which Harappan site?
items.x: Kalibangan shows evidence of an earthquake, besides a ploughed field and fire altars.

items.s: At which site was a signboard of ten Indus signs found?
items.x: The ten-sign signboard is from Dholavira; Lothal has the dockyard and Kalibangan the ploughed field.

items.s: Which Harappan site is known for a dockyard regarded as the world's first tidal port?
items.x: Lothal in Gujarat had a dockyard regarded as the world's first tidal port, along with a bead factory. Dholavira is known for its water reservoirs and signboard, Sutkagendor is the westernmost coastal town, and Chanhudaro for its bead factory without a citadel.

items.s: With which site are skeletons found in wells associated?
items.x: Skeletons in wells are linked with Mohenjo-daro, along with the humped bull seal.

items.s: From which site comes the earliest evidence of a furnace in the Harappan context?
items.x: Kot Bala gives the earliest furnace evidence.

items.s: Which Harappan site is particularly associated with the absence of a citadel, an ink-pot and a cart with a seated driver?
items.x: Chanhudaro is distinguished by its bead-making factory, absence of a citadel, ink-pot and cart with a seated driver.

items.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
items.x: Seven fire altars are associated with Kalibangan, not Rangpur. Rangpur is associated with rice and the Late Harappan Rojdi culture.

items.s: Which Harappan site is correctly matched?
o: Banawali – Largest IVC site in India
items.x: Ropar yielded a steatite seal. Surkotada is linked with pot burials, Rakhigarhi is the largest IVC site in India and Banawali has Mother Goddess figurines.

items.s: Where have a clay model of a plough and a system of radial streets been found?
items.x: Banawali is associated with a clay plough model and radial streets. Kalibangan, in contrast, yielded evidence of an actual ploughed field.

items.s: A dog buried with humans has been found at which Harappan site?
items.x: Ropar yielded a dog buried with humans, a steatite seal and oval pit burials.

items.s: What is Chanhudaro, called the 'Lancashire of India', especially known for?
items.x: Chanhudaro had a bead-making and bangle factory; the dockyard is at Lothal, the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro and seven fire altars at Kalibangan.

items.s: From which site was a cylindrical steatite seal with an alligator motif reported in 2026?
items.x: Rakhigarhi yielded a cylindrical steatite seal with an alligator motif and five signs.

items.s: At which Harappan site was a gold foundry reported in 2026?
items.x: In 2026 Rakhigarhi yielded a gold foundry and a steatite seal with an alligator motif.

items.s: The traces of the cultivation In Harappan Culture were found at:
items.x: Rice husks – the trace of rice cultivation – were found at Lothal and Rangpur; Kalibangan has a ploughed field, but Ropar gives no cultivation evidence, so Lothal and Rangpur is the pair.

items.s: Rice, bajra and sorghum are associated with which Harappan site?
items.x: Rangpur in Saurashtra yielded rice, bajra and sorghum.

items.s: From which site comes the earliest evidence of garlic in the Harappan context?
items.x: Balu has the earliest garlic; Kot Bala has the earliest furnace.

items.s: From which Harappan site was a Persian Gulf seal found?
items.x: A Persian Gulf seal was found at Lothal, a port town.

items.s: An ivory scale in Harappan context was found at –
items.x: An ivory scale was found at Lothal; a shell scale came from Mohenjodaro.

items.s: The measuring scale found at an Indus site is at
items.x: The ivory measuring scale was found at Lothal (a shell scale is also known from Mohenjodaro, but the classic answer is Lothal).

items.s: Which Indus Valley City a scale has been discovered?
items.x: An ivory scale was discovered at Lothal.

items.s: One of the following sites from where the famous bull-seal of Indus Valley Civilization was found-
items.x: The famous humped-bull seal (with the Pashupati seal) comes from Mohenjodaro.

items.s: At which Harappan site was an ivory scale found?
items.x: Lothal yielded an ivory scale besides its dockyard and bead factory.

items.s: Of which material were most Harappan seals made?
items.x: Seals were mostly of steatite; a few were of terracotta, agate and chert.

items.s: What was the commonest shape of Harappan seals?
items.x: Most seals were square; a few were cube, circular or cylindrical.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the Harappan script:
1. It has been deciphered.
2. It was mostly written from right to left.
3. It has about 400+ signs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: The script is pictographic, written right to left with about 400+ signs, and remains undeciphered.

items.s: In which direction was the Harappan script generally written?
items.x: The script ran right to left, with some boustrophedon.

items.s: What was the nature of the Harappan script?
items.x: The Harappan script is pictographic and still undeciphered.

items.s: Which of the following sites has yielded evidence of a double burial?
items.x: Lothal yielded three double (joint) burials in brick-lined graves; Kuntasi is a Harappan port/industrial site, not known for double burial, and the printed explanation (Sinauli graves) does not support Kuntasi.

items.s: What do differences in house size, burial goods and ornaments in the IVC indicate?
items.x: Differences in house size and grave goods point to social stratification in the IVC.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Harappan grave goods?
o: They included pottery, ornaments, mirrors, beads and food
They indicate a belief in an afterlife
Public drains, not grave goods, are the most direct evidence of afterlife belief
items.x: Grave goods such as pottery, ornaments, mirrors, beads and food placed with the dead most directly indicate afterlife belief and status differences; drains say nothing about it.

items.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dog buried with a man — Surkotada
items.x: Double burial, involving two bodies in one grave, is associated with Lothal. Four pot burials belong to Surkotada, the dog burial to Ropar and fractional burial to Mohenjodaro.

items.s: Where were four pot burials found?
items.x: Four pot burials are reported from Surkotada.

items.s: Which burial type – site pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
items.x: Oval-pit and symbolic graves belong to Kalibangan; Lothal is known for double burial.

items.s: To which Harappan site do the Cemetery H and R37 burials belong?
items.x: Coffin burial, Cemetery H and R37 are at Harappa.

items.s: With which site is double burial in the Harappan civilization associated?
items.x: Lothal is known for double burial; Surkotada for pot burials.

items.s: At which Harappan site has coffin burial been found?
items.x: Coffin burial, along with the Cemetery H and R37 burials, belongs to Harappa.

items.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Harappan buildings and polity is correct?
o: Fortified citadels prove that the cities were governed exclusively by warriors.
Planned cities and drainage systems suggest some form of municipal governance.
Large palaces and temples have been conclusively identified in all major cities.
The political system is conclusively known to have been a hereditary monarchy.
items.x: Planned cities and drains suggest municipal governance, while the exact political structure remains uncertain. Citadels may indicate a ruling group, but its composition is debated.

items.s: What do planned cities and drains in the IVC suggest?
items.x: Planned cities and drains indicate municipal governance; the citadel's ruling group is debated.

items.s: Of what does Cemetery R-37 at Harappa provide evidence?
items.x: Cemetery R-37 at Harappa shows burial rites, while fire altars at Kalibangan and Lothal show fire rituals.

items.s: Which of the following was known to the Harappans?
items.x: Mirrors and combs were known to the Harappans.

items.s: Which one of the following features is associated with the Priest-King sculpture of Mohenjodaro?
o: A tribhanga posture with bangles covering both arms
A seated driver holding the reins of a toy cart
A clean-shaven face and a crown with animal horns
A beard, a forehead fillet and a shawl over one shoulder
items.x: The Priest-King is represented as bearded, with a fillet on the forehead and a shawl over one shoulder.

items.s: Which Harappan artefact is correctly matched with its site?
items.x: The copper dog and bird are from Lothal. The Priest-King is from Mohenjodaro, and the nude male torso and dog chasing a deer are from Harappa.

items.s: Who excavated the bronze Dancing Girl in 1926?
items.x: Ernest Mackay excavated the Dancing Girl in 1926 under John Marshall.

items.s: Of which material is the Priest-King sculpture of Mohenjodaro made?
items.x: The Priest-King is of steatite; the Dancing Girl is of bronze.

items.s: Where was the nude male torso of red sandstone found?
items.x: The red sandstone nude male torso comes from Harappa.

items.s: By which process was the Dancing Girl of Mohenjodaro cast?
items.x: The bronze Dancing Girl was made by the lost-wax (cire perdue) method.

items.s: Which of the following describes typical Harappan pottery?
o: Red slip with black painted designs
items.x: Harappan pottery is red slip with black painted designs.

items.s: Which design is NOT typical of painted Harappan pottery?
items.x: Painted designs include pipal leaves, fish scales and intersecting circles; chariots are not among them.

items.s: Lipstick has been found at which Harappan site?
items.x: Lipstick was found at Chanhudaro; dice at Harappa.

items.s: At which Harappan site have dice been found?
items.x: Dice were found at Harappa.

items.s: Where does the bronze figure of a dog chasing a deer come from?
items.x: The bronze 'dog chasing a deer' is from Harappa; the copper dog and bird from Lothal.

items.s: Where was the bronze bull figure of the Harappan civilisation found?
items.x: A bronze bull figure comes from Kalibangan; the copper dog and bird come from Lothal.

items.s:
The worship of Fire in the Indus valley is proved by the discovery of the Fire altar at

a. Surkotada
b. Alamgirpur

c. Kalibangan
d. Chanhudaro
items.x: Fire altars were found at Kalibangan (seven in a row) and Lothal (also Banawali, Rakhigarhi), not at Surkotada or Chanhudaro – so 'c only'.

items.s: At which Harappan site were seven fire altars found?
items.x: Kalibangan had seven fire altars, along with a ploughed field and earthquake evidence.

items.s: Which of the following does not display the continuity of Indus Valley Culture ?
items.x: Wheat and cotton cultivation, Pashupati-Shiva worship and even seal-like symbols on punch-marked coins continued after the IVC, but the Harappan script did not survive and is still undeciphered.

items.s: Bhagwanpura is associated with which of the following?
o: Harappan fire altars and a ploughed field
items.x: Bhagwanpura in Kurukshetra, Haryana, shows Late Harappan and Painted Grey Ware (PGW) cultures overlapping. The port belongs to Lothal, water management to Dholavira and fire altars to Kalibangan.

items.s: Hastinapura can be identified with which one of the following modern cities?
items.x:
Key: Delhi. Strictly, Hastinapur lies in Meerut district (UP), about 100 km from Delhi; Delhi is Indraprastha.
Hastinapura, the Kuru capital, is the option associated with Delhi (Indraprastha) among those given; the site itself lies in Meerut district, UP.

items.s: Karna exercised his divine weapon, given by Indra, to attack one of the following
items.x: In the Mahabharata Karna had to spend Indra's infallible spear (Vasavi Shakti), kept for Arjuna, on Bhima's son Ghatotkacha on the fourteenth night of the war. (Ghatotkacha here is the epic hero, not the Gupta king.)

items.s: What was the name of the Conch of Nakula?
items.x: In the Bhagavad Gita (1.16) Nakula blew the conch Sughosha and Sahadeva Manipushpaka; Panchajanya was Krishna's. (Mahabharata topic, moved.)

items.s: Who narrated the war of Mahabharat to Dhrita Rashtra?
items.x: Sanjaya, given divine sight by Vyasa, narrated the Kurukshetra war to the blind king Dhritarashtra (Bhagavad Gita is his report).

items.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
items.s: The Pancha Kosha Theory of Education was elaborated by
items.x: The five-sheath (pancha kosha) model comes from the Taittiriya Upanishad; in education it is elaborated in Sri Aurobindo's integral education (physical, vital, mental, psychic, spiritual), so the expected answer is Aurobindo.

items.s: Who is known as Radheya in Mahabharatha?
items.x: Karna is called Radheya after his foster mother Radha. Krishna, Arjuna and Dhrishtadyumna have other epithets.

items.s: Who wake up Sri Rama by singing Kausalya Supraja Rama...?
items.x: In the Bala Kanda of the Ramayana, Vishwamitra wakes Rama with 'Kausalya supraja Rama' on the way to his yajna. Vasishtha was the family preceptor.

items.s: One of the sons to Atri, one among the Sapta Rushies (Seven Rushies) and his wife Anasuya.
items.x: Durvasa was a son of Atri and Anasuya (with Dattatreya and Chandra). Vishwamitra, Ashtavakra and Jamadagni were not.

items.s: For how many days Karna was the commander of Kaurava Military during Kurukshetra war?
items.x: In the Mahabharata Karna led the Kaurava army for two days (the 16th and 17th) after Drona, until Arjuna killed him.

items.s: Who was the mother of Shatrughna?
items.x: In the Ramayana, Shatrughna (twin of Lakshmana) was the son of King Dasharatha and Queen Sumitra; Kaikeyi was Bharata's mother.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Animal Husbandry Assist
items.s: The Samaveda is an important source for
items.x: The Samaveda, a collection of Rig Vedic hymns set to melody, is the source of Indian music.

items.s: Which Mahabharata warrior was also known as Gudakesh?
items.x: Gudakesha ('conqueror of sleep') is an epithet of Arjuna in the Mahabharata/Bhagavad Gita.

items.s: Who killed Shakuni in Mahabharat war?
items.x: Sahadeva, the youngest Pandava, killed Shakuni on the 18th day of the Kurukshetra war.

items.s: Who has instigated Ravana to abduct Sita?
items.x: In the Ramayana, Ravana's sister Surpanakha, insulted by Lakshmana, urged Ravana to abduct Sita. Mandodari was Ravana's wife and Tataka a demoness killed by Rama.

items.s: Name the son of Ravan who was killed in the hands of Lord "Hanuma".
items.x: In the Sundara Kanda of Valmiki's Ramayana, Hanuman kills Ravana's young son Aksha Kumara at the Ashoka grove. Indrajit (Meghanada) was killed by Lakshmana; Mahodara and Mahaparshva were Ravana's commanders, not sons killed by Hanuman.

items.s: Who wrote down the epic Mahabharatha while Vyasa was dictating?
items.x: By tradition Ganesha wrote down the Mahabharata as Vyasa dictated it. Shiva, Narada and Vishwakarma are not the scribe.

items.s: In the parlance of Vedic Literature this sentence is said to be prominent one.
items.x: 'Tat tvam asi' (That thou art), a mahavakya of the Chandogya Upanishad, is the celebrated Vedic sentence. The others are later devotional lines.

items.s: Who narrated Bhagavata Puranam to Parikshita Maharaja?
items.x: Sage Shuka (son of Vyasa) narrated the Bhagavata Purana to King Parikshit; Suta later retold it to Shaunaka and the sages. (Off-topic; moved.)

items.s: One among the four was not one of the four wicked.
items.x: The 'dushta chatushtaya' (four wicked ones) of the Mahabharata are Duryodhana, Dussasana, Karna and Sakuni; Sisupala is not one of them.

items.s: Who is Vaikhanasa?
items.x: Vaikhanasa was a sage (maharshi) to whom the Vaikhanasa Agama of temple worship is traced.

items.s: Who is the father of Bhishma?
items.x: Bhishma (Devavrata) was the son of King Shantanu and the river Ganga.

items.s: Eka Vimshathi in Bhagavatham represents this
items.x: 'Ekavimsati' (twenty-one) in the Bhagavatam refers to the 21 avataras of Vishnu listed in its first skandha.

items.s: Sabari was in the Ashram of
items.x: In the Ramayana, Sabari served in the ashram of sage Matanga near Pampa and waited there for Rama. (Moved to ancient literature.)

items.s: During the Vedic period Indra was treated as?
items.x: Indra, called Purandara (breaker of forts), was above all the warlord who led the Aryans to victory; he was also regarded as a rain god, but the warrior role is the one stressed. Agni was the fire god.

items.s:
Select the correct statements about religious beliefs of the Rig Vedic Period :

I. Dyus was a celestial God of the Rig Vedic Aryans similar to Jupiter of the Greeks.

II. Prithvi was considered as the mother of all Gods.

III. Agni was worshipped as the intermediary of taking the offerings to the deities.

IV. Cow sacrifice was also the part of worship.
items.x: I, III and IV: Dyaus (Dyaus pitar) parallels Greek Zeus/Roman Jupiter, Agni carried offerings to the gods, and animal (including cattle) sacrifice was part of worship. II is wrong: Aditi, not Prithvi, was the mother of the gods.

items.s: The religion of early Vedic Aryans was primarily of
items.x: Early Vedic religion was worship of nature (personified forces) through open-air yajnas; there were no images and bhakti came much later.

items.s: In context on Indian culture 'Rita' means
items.x: Rita is the natural (cosmic) order or natural law, upheld by Varuna.

items.s: Rig-vedic religion was–
items.x: Rig Vedic religion was polytheistic (many nature gods, each praised in turn as supreme – henotheism); it was not monotheistic or monistic.

items.s: The name of the mountain which was used to churn Ksheera Sagara
items.x: In the Samudra Manthan legend the gods and asuras used Mount Mandara as the churning rod and the serpent Vasuki as the rope to churn the Kshira Sagara. Off-topic (mythology), moved.

items.s: Who is the Guru (Teacher) of demons (Rakshasulu)?
items.x: Shukracharya (Shukra, son of Bhrigu) is the guru of the asuras/rakshasas; Brihaspati is the guru of the devas, and Vibhishana and Mairavana are Ramayana characters. (Off-topic; moved.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
items.s: The branch of philosophy that is concerned with reasoning is called
items.x: Logic is the branch of philosophy concerned with the principles of correct reasoning (in Indian thought, the Nyaya school).

items.s: What is the name of Vasishta's Cow?
items.x:
Most books and keys: Nandini (Mahabharata). The Valmiki Ramayana calls the same cow Shabala (Sabala).
Vasishtha's wish-fulfilling cow, coveted by Vishvamitra, is called Nandini (daughter of Kamadhenu) in most books and keys. Off-topic (epics), moved.

items.s: On what was Rig Vedic religion centred?
o: Male nature gods and open-air yajnas
items.x: Rig Vedic religion featured male nature gods like Indra, Agni and Varuna and open-air yajnas, with no temples or idols.

items.s: To which deity is the entire 9th Mandala of the Rigveda devoted?
items.x: Soma has the whole 9th Mandala of the Rigveda.

items.s: Of what is Varuna the upholder in the Rigveda?
items.x: Varuna is the upholder of cosmic order; Agni is the god of fire and sacrifice and Indra the warrior god.

items.s: Which Mandala of the Rigveda is wholly devoted to Soma?
items.x: The whole of Mandala IX is devoted to Soma, the sacred drink.

items.s: Which of the following describes the religious outlook of the Rig Vedic people?
o: Monotheism with exclusive worship of one god
Ancestor worship centred on royal tombs
Naturalistic polytheism with each god praised as supreme in turn
items.x: Rig Vedic religion was naturalistic polytheism. Its tendency to regard each god as supreme in turn is called Henotheism or Kathenotheism.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rig Vedic worship?
o: Temples and idols formed the normal basis of worship
Worship was conducted through hymns and yajnas in the open air
Its principal aims included cattle, sons and victory
The cult of the domestic hearth was significant
items.x: Temples and idols were absent in Rig Vedic worship, which used hymns and open-air yajnas for material ends such as cattle, sons and victory.

items.s: Which Rig Vedic god was called Purandara, 'destroyer of forts'?
items.x: Indra, called Purandara, is the most mentioned Rig Vedic god with about 250 hymns.

items.s: Which Vedic god was called Ritasyagopa, the guardian of Rita (cosmic order)?
items.x: Varuna guards Rita, the cosmic and natural order, and is therefore called Ritasyagopa.

items.s: Which one of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
items.x: Vishnu was a minor deity in the Rig Vedic period and is associated with three hymns, not about 250. About 250 hymns are associated with Indra.

items.s: Of whom was Dyaus, the celestial father, regarded as the counterpart?
items.x: Dyaus was the sky or celestial father and corresponded to Greek Zeus and Roman Jupiter.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rig Vedic gods?
o: Agni ranked second among the Rig Vedic gods
Agni acted as intermediary between humans and gods
Agni was the deity who upheld Rita
items.x: Agni was second in rank and the intermediary between humans and gods; it was Varuna, not Agni, who upheld Rita.

items.s: In the Rigveda, which deity was regarded as the mother of the gods?
items.x: Aditi was the mother of the gods; calling Prithvi the mother of all gods is a common error.

items.s: How many hymns of the Rigveda are addressed to Vishnu?
items.x: Vishnu was a minor god with 3 hymns, against about 250 for Indra and 200 for Agni.

items.s: Which Rig Vedic deity is associated with forests?
items.x: Aranyani was the forest deity; Pushan was of cattle and roads, Prithvi the earth and Parjanya rain.

items.s: What is the Rigvedic practice of praising each god in turn as the supreme one called?
items.x: Rigvedic religion was henotheistic (kathenotheism): each god was praised as supreme in turn.

items.s: Which Rigvedic goddess personified the dawn?
items.x: Usha was the goddess of dawn; Aditi was the mother of the gods and Aranyani the forest goddess.

items.s: Which Rigvedic god was associated with cattle and roads?
items.x: Pushan was the god of cattle and roads; Parjanya was the rain god.

items.s: In Pali texts, the city is known as:
items.x: Pali texts use 'nigama' for a town (market town) beside 'nagara' for a large city; the printed key takes Nigam. 'Pur' is the Vedic term for a fortified settlement.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Bimbisara belonged to the ____ dynasty.
items.x: Bimbisara belonged to the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha; Pradyota was a dynasty of Avanti.

items.s: Nanda clan are followers of which clan?
items.x: The Nandas succeeded (followed) the Shishunaga dynasty: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya.

items.s: Who defeated and assimilated the Vajjis into the empire of Magadha?
items.x: Ajatashatru defeated the Vajji confederacy after a 16-year war, using deceit, and annexed Vaishali to Magadha.

items.s: In which century did the first Magadhan Empire rise?
items.x: The first Magadhan empire rose in the 6th century BC under Bimbisara (Haryanka), a contemporary of the Buddha.

items.s: What was the name of the dynasty of Ajatshatru?
items.x: Ajatashatru, son and successor of Bimbisara, belonged to the Haryanka dynasty.

items.s: Between the sixth and the fourth centuries BCE, ______ became the most powerful mahajanapada.
items.x: Between the 6th and 4th centuries BCE Magadha became the most powerful Mahajanapada (iron, elephants, fertile land, rivers).

items.s: Which one of the following was initially the most powerful city-state in India in the 6th century B.C.?
items.x: Of the four powers, Magadha emerged as the most powerful in the 6th century BC and founded the first empire; Gandhara, Kamboja and Kashi did not.

items.s: Which ruler had made Pataliputra the capital of his empire for the first time?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Udayin); it is added as option 5.
No printed option is right: Udayin (Haryanka) first made Pataliputra the capital of Magadha, moving it from Rajgriha. The Nandas already ruled from there before Chandragupta Maurya, and Ashoka, Chandragupta Vikramaditya and Kanishka came later still. The printed key (Chandragupta Maurya) is wrong.

items.s: Who ended the power of Avanti and made Magadha supreme?
items.x: Shishunaga, founder of the Shishunaga dynasty, ended the power of Avanti.

items.s: During whose reign was the Second Buddhist Council held at Vaishali?
items.x: Kalashoka of the Shishunaga dynasty was associated with the Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali.

items.s: Who shifted the capital of Magadha from Rajagriha to Pataliputra?
items.x: Udayin moved the capital of Magadha from Rajagriha to Pataliputra.

items.s: Which ruler is treated as the founder of the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha?
items.x: Bimbisara (544-492 BCE) founded the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha. Ajatashatru and Udayin were his Haryanka successors, while Shishunaga founded the next dynasty.

items.s: Which territory did Bimbisara receive in part as dowry from Kosala?
items.x: Bimbisara's marriage alliance with Kosala brought part of Kashi as dowry; he also allied with the Lichchhavis and Madra.

items.s: What was 'Mahashilakantaka', a weapon of Ajatashatru?
items.x: Mahashilakantaka was a catapult; the chariot fitted with a mace was the Rathamusala.

items.s: Which Nanda ruler was known as Ekarat?
items.x: Mahapadma Nanda was called Ekarat; Dhana Nanda was the last Nanda ruler.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the Magadhan dynasties:
1. The Shishunaga dynasty came after the Haryanka dynasty.
2. The Nanda dynasty came before the Shishunaga dynasty.
3. The Maurya dynasty followed the Nanda dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: The sequence is Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda and Maurya, so the Nandas came after the Shishunagas (statement 2 is wrong).

items.s: Who ruled Magadha at the time of Alexander's invasion of north-west India?
items.x: Magadha was then ruled by the Nandas under Dhana Nanda, the last Nanda king. Mahapadma Nanda was the earlier Nanda empire-builder, Chandragupta Maurya came to power later (c. 321 BCE) and Kalashoka was a Shishunaga ruler.

items.s: What does the Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela indicate?
o: Alexander built a canal connecting the Ganga and Son
Nandaraja dug a canal which was later extended by Kharavela
Shishunaga constructed irrigation works in Avanti
Bimbisara constructed a canal in Anga
items.x: The Hathigumpha inscription states that a canal dug by Nandaraja, identified with Mahapadma Nanda, was extended by Kharavela. It also indicates Nanda control over Kalinga.

items.s: Which was the first non-Kshatriya dynasty of Magadha?
items.x: The Nandas were the first non-Kshatriya dynasty.

items.s: Bimbisara annexed which Mahajanapada?
items.x: Bimbisara took Anga; Ajatashatru later defeated the Vajjis.

items.s: How long did Ajatashatru's war with the Vajjis last?
items.x: Ajatashatru beat the Vajjis after a 16-year war by sowing dissension.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Magadhan rulers?
o: Udayin moved the capital to Pataliputra
Kalashoka held the Second Buddhist Council
Bimbisara belonged to the Shishunaga dynasty
items.x: Bimbisara belonged to the Haryanka dynasty, not the Shishunaga dynasty.

items.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shishunaga destroyed the power of Avanti.
2. Kalashoka of the Shishunaga dynasty held the Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Shishunaga ended Avanti's power and his successor Kalashoka held the Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali.

items.s: What was 'Rathamusala', a weapon used by Ajatashatru?
items.x: Ajatashatru used the Rathamusala, a chariot with a mace, and the Mahashilakantaka, a catapult, against the Vajjis.

items.s: Which Nanda king took the image of Jina from Kalinga?
items.x: Mahapadma Nanda took the statue of Jina from Kalinga, which shows Nanda control over Kalinga.

items.s: With which of the following did Bimbisara NOT form a marriage alliance?
items.x: Bimbisara married into Kosala, the Lichchhavis and Madra; Avanti under Pradyota was his rival.

items.s: Which of the following was NOT a factor in the rise of Magadha?
o: Availability of iron ore for tools and weapons
Dependence on a purely pastoral economy
items.x: Magadha benefited from fertile agriculture, iron resources, elephants and rivers. Dependence on a purely pastoral economy was not a stated factor in its rise.

items.s: Pataliputra stood at the confluence of the Ganga and which river?
items.x: Pataliputra was established at the Ganga-Son confluence; the earlier capital Rajagriha was protected by five hills.

items.s: To which period is Bimbisara's reign dated?
items.x: Bimbisara ruled 544-492 BCE; Ajatashatru 492-460 BCE.

items.s: By which period had Magadha become the most powerful Mahajanapada?
items.x: Magadha became the most powerful Mahajanapada during the 6th to 4th centuries BCE.

items.s: Who founded Pataliputra?
items.x: Pataliputra was founded by the Haryanka king Ajatashatru; his son Udayin moved the capital there from Rajgriha.

items.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pataliputra was founded by Ajatashatru.
2. Udayin moved the capital of Magadha from Rajgriha to Pataliputra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Ajatashatru founded Pataliputra and Udayin shifted the capital there from Rajgriha.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the founding of capitals?
o: Ajatashatru established Pataliputra as a fortified settlement.
Udayin shifted the capital from Rajagriha to Pataliputra.
Firoz Shah Tughlaq established Tughlaqabad in Delhi.
Udayin was the successor of Ajatashatru.
items.x: Tughlaqabad was established by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, not Firoz Shah Tughlaq; Ajatashatru fortified Pataliputra and his successor Udayin shifted the capital there.

items.s: 'Kalpasutra' is a text related to
items.x: The Kalpasutra of Bhadrabahu is a Jain canonical text on the lives of the Tirthankaras. The Vedic Kalpa Sutras share the name but the exam item means the Jain work.

items.s: Which Mauryan ruler is traditionally associated with Bhadrabahu in the southward spread of Jainism?
items.x: Chandragupta Maurya adopted Jainism and is traditionally associated with Bhadrabahu in its southward movement.

items.s: Of which faith was Kharavela a follower?
items.x: Kharavela was a Jain, not an Ajivika; the Ajivikas go back to Makkhali Gosala.

items.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Amoghavarsha I was a disciple of the Jain Acharya Jinasena.
Heliodorus was associated with Bhagavata Religion.
Kharavela of Kalinga was a follower of the Ajivika sect.
items.x: Option C is incorrect: Kharavela of Kalinga was a Jain, as his Hathigumpha inscription shows; the Ajivika sect was founded by Makkhali Gosala. Amoghavarsha I, Heliodorus and the Guptas are correctly described.

items.s:
With reference to the cultural history of India, consider the following pairs.

I. Parivrajaka – Renuncient and Wanderer

II. Shramana – Priest with a high status

III. Upasaka – Lay follower of Buddhism
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
items.x: Parivrajaka = wanderer/renunciant and Upasaka = lay follower of Buddhism are correct; Shramana means a seeker or ascetic, not a high-status priest (UPSC 2020).

items.s:
Which of the following kingdoms were associated with the life of the Buddha?
1. Avanti
2. Gandhara
3. Kosala
4. Magadha
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
items.x: Kosala (Shravasti, Jetavana; Shakyas under Kosala) and Magadha (Bodh Gaya, Rajagriha) were central to the Buddha's life; Avanti and Gandhara were not directly associated – so 3 and 4 only (UPSC 2015).

items.s: Which of the following religions is non-theocentric?
items.x: Buddhism is non-theocentric: it does not centre on a creator God. Hinduism, Christianity and Islam are theistic. Moved to the Buddhism row.

items.s: Second Buddhist Council was held at which place?
items.x: The Second Buddhist Council met at Vaishali (c. 383 BCE) under Kalashoka. Rajgriha hosted the First and Pataliputra the Third.

items.s: After the Mahaparinirvana of Lord Buddha, the first Buddhist Council was held at
items.x: The First Buddhist Council met in the Saptaparni cave at Rajgriha just after the Buddha's death (c. 483 BCE), under Ajatashatru, presided over by Mahakassapa.

items.s: ‘Saptaparni Cave’ is situated in –
items.x: The Saptaparni cave is at Rajgriha (Rajgir), the venue of the First Buddhist Council.

items.s: A Buddhist Council during the reign of Ashoka was held at
items.x: The Third Buddhist Council (c. 250 BCE) met at Pataliputra under Ashoka, presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa.

items.s: The first Buddhist Council was held during the reign of -
items.x: The First Buddhist Council at Rajgriha was held under Ajatashatru, who hosted it just after the Buddha's death; Bimbisara was already dead.

items.s: With whom is the Madhyamika school of Buddhism associated?
items.x: Madhyamika is Nagarjuna's school; Syadvada is linked with Kundakundacharya, Dvaita with Madhvacharya and Purva Mimamsa with Kumarila Bhatta.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Places of worship built by Bouddhas (Buddhists) are called as
items.x: A chaitya (chaitya-shala or chaitya-griha) is the Buddhist prayer hall – the place of worship; a vihara is the monks' residence, and guhas and toranas are caves and gateways.

items.src: Assistant Executive Engineers in Electrical Engineering Scre
items.s:
Which of the following statements regarding 'Stupa' are correct?

a. They are pre Buddhist structures.

b. They are built on the relics of Buddha.

c. They are built as objects of devotion by Buddhist monasteries.

d. They are built to commemorate important events in Buddha's life
Select the correct code from the following:
items.at: All of the above (a, b, c and d)
items.x: All four are correct: burial mounds (stupas) predate Buddhism; Buddhist stupas enshrine relics, are built as objects of devotion by monasteries, and mark events of the Buddha's life.

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: The Ajanta Caves are related to which religion?
items.x: The Ajanta caves (2nd c. BCE–6th c. CE) are Buddhist chaityas and viharas. Jain caves are at Ellora and Udayagiri, not Ajanta.

items.s: Which of the following laid the foundation of idol worship in the country?
items.x: Image worship is credited to Buddhism, whose Mahayana phase made the Buddha image (Gandhara and Mathura) the centre of worship; the Vedic religion was aniconic. Jainism's early Jina images are the tempting alternative, but books key Buddhism.

items.s: Palitana temple is located near –
items.x: The Palitana Jain temples on Shatrunjaya hill are in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat. Mount Abu has the Dilwara temples.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
items.s: An ancient Buddhist site in which of the following districts was discovered through excavation by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) between 1994 and 2001 and has now been taken up for conservation work by ASI?
items.x: Kanaganahalli (on the Bhima, Kalaburagi district, Karnataka) was excavated by the ASI in 1994-2001; its 1st-3rd century CE stupa has the stone portrait of Ashoka. (Off-topic; moved.)

items.s: Use of which language, placing religious teaching beyond common people, encouraged the rise of heterodox sects?
items.x: Sanskrit-centred religious practice, along with costly yajnas, animal sacrifice and dissatisfaction with ritualism, encouraged heterodox sects.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of the rise of heterodox sects?
o: Vedic sacrifices consumed cattle needed for iron-plough farming
Mahavira and Buddha were both Kshatriyas
Newly rich Vaishyas favoured the Vedic sacrificial religion
items.x: The newly rich Vaishyas wanted higher status and did not favour the Vedic sacrificial religion; the other three statements are correct.

items.s: Who popularised the Ajivika sect?
items.x: Makkhali Gosala popularised the Ajivika sect. Nanda Vachcha is associated with its foundation and Kisa Sankichcha with its subsequent leadership.

items.s: What was the central doctrine of the Ajivikas?
o: The immortality of the physical body
items.x: The Ajivikas followed Niyati, or strict fatalism, and rejected karma and free will.

items.s: Who gifted the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas?
items.x: Ashoka and Dasharatha gifted the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas.

items.s: Who was the founder of the Ajivika sect?
items.x: Nanda Vachcha founded the Ajivikas; Makkhali Gosala popularised the sect.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the rise of heterodox sects:
1. Kshatriyas resented the dominance of Brahmins.
2. Newly rich Vaishyas sought higher status.
3. Vedic sacrifices conserved the cattle needed for farming.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Sacrifices consumed the cattle needed for iron-plough farming, so statement 3 is wrong.

items.s: Who was the founder of the Ajivika sect?
items.x: The Ajivika sect, which believed in determinism, was founded by Makkhali Gosala.

items.s: Which Achaemenid ruler annexed Punjab and Sindh around 516 BCE?
items.x: Cyrus began the Persian invasions, and Darius I annexed Punjab and Sindh c. 516 BCE.

items.s: Which ruler of Taxila submitted to Alexander?
items.x: Ambhi of Taxila submitted to Alexander, whereas Porus fought him at the Battle of Hydaspes.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
items.x: The Kalinga War was fought in 261 BC; c. 383 BC is the date of the Second Council.

items.s: Which cultural development is associated with the Achaemenid Persian presence in north-western India?
o: Introduction of Brahmi script from the Deccan
Replacement of all local scripts by Greek
items.x: The Persian presence contributed to the spread of the Kharosthi script in the north-western region.

items.s: In which year did Alexander die at Babylon?
items.x: Alexander crossed the Indus in 326 BCE and died at Babylon in 323 BCE.

items.s: On the banks of which river was the Battle of Hydaspes fought?
items.x: Hydaspes is the Jhelum, where Alexander fought Porus in 326 BCE.

items.s: Which Persian ruler began the Achaemenid invasions of India?
items.x: Cyrus began the Achaemenid invasions; Darius I later annexed Punjab and Sindh.

items.s: Which river marked the limit of Alexander's advance in India?
items.x: The Beas marked the limit of Alexander's advance; the Jhelum is the Hydaspes.

items.s: In which year did Alexander cross the Indus?
items.x: Alexander crossed the Indus in 326 BCE and died at Babylon in 323 BCE.

items.x: The land from the Vindhyas to the Krishna was called Dakshinapatha (the southern route/region). Off-topic (ancient Indian history), moved.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
items.s: The 'Bavikonda Buddhist Complex' is located in which of the following districts of Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: Bavikonda, a Buddhist monastic complex (3rd c. BCE–2nd c. CE) on a hill near Visakhapatnam, is in Visakhapatnam district. Off-topic (AP history), moved.

items.s: Which of the following is true of the date of the Dharanikota sculptures?
o: Later than those of Sanchi and Bharhut
Older than those of Sanchi and Bharhut
items.x: Dharanikota sculptures, in the Amaravati region, are described as older than those of Sanchi and Bharhut.

items.s: The great law-giver of ancient times was –
items.x: Manu, author of the Manusmriti, is the great law-giver of ancient India; Ambedkar was called the 'Modern Manu'. Moved to ancient history.

items.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gupta rulers – Tamil devotees of Vishnu
items.x: Heliodorus set up the Garuda pillar at Besnagar as a Bhagavata; the Alvars worshipped Vishnu, the Nayanars Shiva, and the Gupta kings took the title Parama-bhagavata.

items.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the given rulers of ancient India?
items.x: Ashoka (c. 268-232 BCE) came first, then the Indo-Greek Milinda/Menander (c. 165-130 BCE), then the Kushana Kanishka (from 78 or 127 CE).

items.s: Who is regarded as the founder of Satavahana dynasty?
items.x: The Satavahana founder was Simuka (Srimukha). Satakarni I was his successor and Naganika Satakarni's queen.

items.s: Which of the following statements is not true about the Satavahanas?
o: They were described as Andhra Brithyas in Puranas
They issued bilingual coins in Prakrit and Dravidian Script
They were patrons of Buddhism and Hinduism
They had matrimonial alliance with Kakatiyas
items.x: The Satavahanas (c. 1st c. BCE-3rd c. CE) could not have had marriage ties with the Kakatiyas (12th-14th c.); they are called Andhrabhrityas in the Puranas, issued bilingual Prakrit-Tamil coins and patronised both Buddhism and Vedic religion.

items.s: In which of the following present-day places in Andhra Pradesh did Satavahana empire exist in ancient times?
items.x: Amaravati (Dhanyakataka) was a Satavahana centre, with the Mahachaitya and their later capital; Kadapa, Palakollu and Anantapuram are not Satavahana sites.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: There was a frequent shifting of capitals. Which one of the following was never used as a Capital city by the Satvahana rulers?
items.x: Pataliputra was the Magadhan (Mauryan, Gupta) capital and never a Satavahana capital; Dharanikota (Dhanyakataka), Junnar and Paithan (Pratishthana) were Satavahana seats.

items.s: The ruler who was described as Trisamudra-dhipati was
items.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni, 'whose horses drank the waters of three seas', is given the title Trisamudradhipati (Thrisamudrapati) in the Rocket sheets; Pulakesin II was 'lord of the three Maharashtras' and Vikramaditya VI 'Tribhuvanamalla'.

items.s: The Satavahanas were
items.x: The Satavahanas were Brahmins: the Nasik inscription calls Gautamiputra Satakarni 'Ekabrahmana'.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: The Andhras, mentioned in the writings of Greek writer Pliny, were also known as the ____.
items.x: Pliny (a Roman, not Greek, writer) in his Natural History describes the Andhras as a powerful people with 30 walled towns and a large army; the Puranas call the Satavahanas 'Andhras' or 'Andhrabhrityas'. Cheras, Cholas and Pallavas are Tamil or later powers.

items.src: Social and Culture History & Welfare Programmes paper 2019
items.s: The Andhras, mentioned in the writings of Greek writer Pliny, were also known as the
items.x: The Andhras whom Pliny describes (30 walled towns, a great army) are identified with the Satavahanas, called Andhras in the Puranas; the Cheras, Cholas and Pallavas are not.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Welfare & Developm
items.s:
Consider the following statements:

A. Goutamiputra Satakarni was kind to his subjects and a father to his people

B. Goutamiputra's son and successor was Goutamiputra Yagnasri
Of the above, the correct statements are
o: Both A and B are incorrect
items.x: The Nasik prashasti praises Gautamiputra Satakarni as caring for his subjects like a father, so A is right. His son and successor was Vasishthiputra Pulumavi; Yajnasri Satakarni came much later, so B is wrong.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s:
A: The capital of the Satavahanas, Prathisthanapuram, was located in Western Deccan.
R: It was strategically chosen to resist foreign invasions and connect the Southern delta with the Western coast.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: Pratishthana (Paithan) on the Godavari in the western Deccan was the Satavahana capital. The key also accepts R: the site linked the Godavari–Krishna delta with the western ports.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: In which place, coins of Sathavahana founder ruler 'Simukha' were found in large number?
items.x: Coins of Simuka, founder of the Satavahana dynasty, were found in large numbers at Kotilingala (Karimnagar).

items.src: Assistant Executive Engineers in Electrical Engineering Scre
items.s: Amravati, the designated capital of Andhra Pradesh, was historical capital of:
items.x: Amaravati (ancient Dhanyakataka) was a capital of the Satavahanas.

items.s: One of the major towns of the Godavari region in the Satavahana kingdom was:
items.x: Pratishthana (Paithan) on the Godavari was a major Satavahana town and capital. Arikamedu (Puducherry), Korkai (Tamil Nadu) and Maski (Karnataka) lie outside the Godavari region.

items.s: One of the major towns of the Godavari region in the Satavahana kingdom was:
items.x: Pratishthana (Paithan) on the Godavari was a leading Satavahana town. Arikamedu, Korkai and Maski are outside the Godavari region.

items.s: Who wrote the book 'Yogasara'?
items.x: Yogasara is listed among the works of Acharya Nagarjuna in the APPSC key and NextGen notes. Kundakundacharya wrote Samayasara, Pravachanasara and Niyamasara, not Yogasara. The printed key (Kundakundacharya) is wrong.

items.src: Social and Culture History & Welfare Programmes paper 2019
items.s: Under the Satvahana dynasty, which one of the following were not the feudal chiefs?
items.x: Maharathis, Mahabhojas and Mahasenapatis were Satavahana feudatories; Mahajanapadas were the 16 states of the 6th century BC, not feudal chiefs.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: Which one of the following statements is correct about the prevalent practice of the adoption of metronymy during the Satvahana and Ikshvakus rule?
o: High social status accorded to women.
Age old practice of enslaving women
items.x: Metronymics such as Gautamiputra and Vasishthiputra show the high social status of women (mothers) under the Satavahanas and Ikshvakus; it does not mean women held all finances or were weak rulers. Off-topic, moved to Satavahanas.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of AP and Welfare Programmes 201
items.s: ____ were the first native Indian dynasty to issue their own coins with the portraits of the rulers.
items.x: The Satavahanas were the first native Indian dynasty to issue coins with the ruler's portrait, from Gautamiputra/Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, copying the Western Kshatrapas; the Ikshvakus, Eastern Chalukyas and Pallavas came later.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20

items.x: The Satavahanas were the first native Indian dynasty to issue coins with the ruler's portrait, from Gautamiputra/Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, copying the Western Kshatrapas; the Ikshvakus, Eastern Chalukyas and Pallavas came later.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Which of the below mentioned insignia is mostly found on the Sathavahana coins
items.x: Of the options only the ship (nouka) is a Satavahana coin device – Yajnasri Satakarni's ship-mast coins show sea trade (Satavahana coins also carry the Ujjain symbol, elephant, horse). Lakshmi and Garuda belong to Gupta coins.

items.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the rule of Satavahanas:

A. For administrative purposes, the empire was divided into a number of Aharas or Rashtras.

B. Salt was a state monopoly.
Of the above, the correct statements are
items.x: The Satavahana kingdom was divided into aharas (rashtras) under amatyas, and their land grants exempt the donee from the royal salt right, showing salt was a state monopoly; so both A and B.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: Hala wrote Gathasaptasati in ____ language.
items.x: Hala's Gathasaptasati (Gaha Sattasai) was written in Maharashtri Prakrit, the court language of the Satavahanas.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: The Official Language of the Satavahanas was
items.x: Satavahana inscriptions and coins use Prakrit, their official language; Sanskrit and Pali were not their state language.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: The first paintings found in India belong to which period
items.x: The earliest surviving historic paintings in India, in Ajanta caves 9 and 10, date from the Satavahana period (2nd c. BCE). Gupta, Chalukya and Paramara paintings are later.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s:
What were the key reasons behind the creation of magnificent Buddhist stupas, caves, chaityas, and viharas during the historical period in South India?

1. Patronage by powerful dynasties like the Satavahanas and Ikshvakus.

2. Geographical aspects of the Deccan Plateau provided easy access to local stone and raw materials.

3. Presence of rivers like Godavari and Krishna and others, supported logistical needs and long worker stays during construction.

4. Bhakti movement leaders funded cave constructions to promote sectarian tolerance.
items.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are right: royal patronage (Satavahanas, Ikshvakus), local stone of the Deccan and the Krishna–Godavari rivers explain the stupas and caves. Statement 4 is wrong – the Bhakti movement came later and funded no Buddhist caves.

items.s: The religion adopted by the Satavahanas
items.x: The Satavahanas were Brahmanas who revived Vedic religion, so Hinduism (Brahmanism) was their religion; they also patronised Buddhism. Jainism was not their faith.

items.s: The temple here has the oldest shivalinga in Andhra Pradesh
items.x: The Parasurameswara temple at Gudimallam (Chittoor/Tirupati district) has the oldest Shiva linga (c. 2nd–1st century BCE) in Andhra Pradesh and India.

items.s: Where is the famous Shiva lingam that shows Lord Shiva in a lingam?
items.x: The Gudimallam lingam (Chittoor district, now Tirupati district) shows Shiva standing in relief on the lingam itself; it is the oldest Shiva lingam of Andhra (Satavahana period).

items.s: Where is the oldest Shivalinga of ancient Andhra located?
items.x: The oldest Shivalinga mentioned is located at Gudimallam in Chittoor district.

items.s: Which dynasty made Vedic religion official, as seen in the Nanaghat inscription?
items.x: The Satavahanas made Vedic religion official; Nanaghat invokes Indra, Vasudeva, Surya and others.

items.s: Gudimallam, the oldest Shiva lingam in Andhra Pradesh, is in which district?
items.x: Gudimallam is in Chittoor district and dates to the Satavahana era.

items.s: For which of the following is Gudimallam, of the Satavahana era, noted in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The earliest known Buddhist stupa in India
The first Harappan fire altar in South India
The oldest Shaivite temple in Andhra Pradesh and a very early Shiva lingam
items.x: Gudimallam in Chittoor district, of the Satavahana era, has the oldest Shiva lingam and Shaivite temple in Andhra Pradesh.

items.src: APPSC Group-II (Mains) Paper-II Social History & Constitutio
items.s: Who was the last Ikshavaku ruler?
items.x: Rudrapurushadatta was the last known ruler of the Ikshvaku dynasty of Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda).

items.s: Which Ikshvaku king had a wife who was the princess of Ujjain?
items.x: Virapurushadatta married Mahadevi Rudradhara-bhattarika of the Saka Kshatrapa house of Ujjain; Chamtamula, Ehuvala Chamtamula and Rudrapurushadatta had no Ujjain wife.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: The stone pillar inscriptions are reliable source of information. The iron pillar at ____ does not provide information about Ikshvakus.
items.x: Ikshvaku records come from Andhra sites such as Nagarjunakonda, Jaggayyapeta and Amaravati; the pillar at Vaishali (Bihar) is Ashokan and says nothing about the Ikshvakus. (The Ikshvaku records are on stone; the 'iron pillar' wording is loose.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s: In which district is the ancient historical site Yeleswaram situated?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Nalgonda (now in Telangana)); it is added as option 5.
The ancient site of Yeleswaram, an Ikshvaku-period town built by the commander Elisri and a source of Roman coins, is in Nalgonda district (now Telangana), submerged by the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir. None of the printed districts is correct; the Yeleswaram in East Godavari (now Kakinada district) is a modern town. (Moved: Ikshvakus row.)

items.s: Who was the last ruler of the Ikshvaku dynasty of Andhra?
items.x: The 2019 key names Rudra Purushadatta as the last Ikshvaku ruler. Vasishthiputra Chamtamula founded the line. Virapurushadatta and Ehuvala Chamtamula were earlier rulers who came before him.

items.s: Who founded the Ikshvaku dynasty of Andhra?
items.x: The Ikshvaku line was founded by Vasishthiputra Chamtamula; Rudra Purushadatta was its last ruler.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
items.s: Which queen of the Ikshvaku dynasty is known from inscriptions for building Buddhist monuments?
items.x: Camtisiri (Chamtisiri), sister of Vasishthiputra Chamtamula and aunt of Virapurushadatta, is the Ikshvaku queen known from Nagarjunakonda inscriptions for building Buddhist monuments. Rudrama was a Kakatiya, Gautami Balashri a Satavahana queen.

items.s: What is the real name of Indrajit?
items.x: Indrajit, Ravana's son, was born Meghanada; he got the name Indrajit after defeating Indra. Akshakumara was another son of Ravana.

items.s: In which district is Nagarjunakonda located?
items.x:
Guntur district was split in April 2022 — Nagarjunakonda (Macherla area) is now in Palnadu district (general knowledge, not checked)
Nagarjunakonda (Ikshvaku capital Vijayapuri) is listed under Guntur district; Nalgonda only shares the Nagarjuna Sagar dam (now Palnadu district, carved out of Guntur in 2022).

items.s: 'Nagarjuna Konda' is located in the district of
items.x:
Guntur district was split on 4 Apr 2022 — Nagarjunakonda is now in Palnadu district (AP district reorganisation; Wikipedia 'Nagarjunakonda').
Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri of the Ikshvakus) lies in Macherla mandal on the right bank of the Krishna, in Guntur district (now Palnadu), not in Nalgonda, which holds only the Nagarjuna Sagar dam's left side.

items.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler performed the Ashvamedha, Rajasuya, Vajapeya and Agnistoma sacrifices, with an Ashvamedha altar found at Nagarjunakonda?
items.x: The Ikshvaku king Santamula performed Ashvamedha, Rajasuya, Vajapeya and Agnistoma; an Ashvamedha altar exists at Nagarjunakonda. Gautamiputra and Yajnasri Satakarni were Satavahanas, and Kharavela was the Kalinga king of the Hathigumpha inscription.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
items.s: Which river's banks saw the flourishing of Buddhist architectural activity under the Ikshvakus?
items.x: The Ikshvakus' capital Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda) stood on the Krishna, where their queens patronised great Buddhist stupas and viharas. The Godavari, Tungabhadra and Pennar are not the Ikshvaku centres.

items.src: APPSC Group-II Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I 2017
items.s: In which district the Bhairava Konda (Kona) of Andhra Pradesh does exist?
items.x:
the area now falls in the new Markapuram district, carved out of Prakasam (web search summary, Wikipedia).
The Bhairavakona rock-cut cave temples (Nallamala hills, near Kothapalli) are in Prakasam district.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s:
Which of the following statements about the social history of Andhra Pradesh is/are correct?

A. The social structure of ancient Andhra Pradesh was predominantly influenced by the Vedic caste system.

B. The Satavahana dynasty played a crucial role in promoting Buddhism in the region.

C. Andhra Pradesh was traditionally a matrilineal society, where lineage and inheritance were passed through the mother's side.

D. The major language spoken in the region historically was Sanskrit, which was used in all social and religious practices.
items.x: Ancient Andhra society followed the Vedic varna order (A) and the Satavahanas, though Brahmanical, patronised Buddhism (B). Andhra was not traditionally matrilineal, and Prakrit and later Telugu, not Sanskrit alone, were used, so 'A and B only'.

items.s: Which place is the main kshetra of Goddess Vasavi?
items.x: Penugonda is the main kshetra of Goddess Vasavi (APPSC G2 2019 area).

items.s: Which of the following city was not the capital of the Guptas?
items.x: Gupta capitals were Pataliputra, with Ayodhya, Prayaga and Ujjayini (Chandragupta II's second capital) also named; Varanasi was never a Gupta capital.

items.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-I Panchayat Secretary /
items.s: Who of the following Chinese pilgrims to India, gave us some information about the first Gupta ruler ?
items.x: I-Tsing (late 7th century) records that Maharaja Sri Gupta built a temple for Chinese pilgrims near Mrigasikhavana – the only Chinese mention of the first Gupta ruler. Fa-Hien named no king and Hiuen Tsang wrote of Harsha.

items.src: Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional Servic
items.s: Which period is called Golden Age?
items.x: The Gupta period (c. 320-550 CE) is called the Golden Age of ancient India for its art, literature and science (Kalidasa, Aryabhata). The Maurya, Kushan and Mughal periods are not given this name.

items.src: Indian History previous paper (header not legible)
items.s: Skanda Gupta had not conquered one of the following rulers.
items.x: Skandagupta's Bhitari pillar records victories over the Pushyamitras (read here as 'Sungas') and the Hunas, and Vakataka pressure is also linked to his reign; no Kalinga conquest is recorded. So the Kalingas is the expected answer.

items.s: The term "Arthika" in early medieval economy refers to
o: a rent free village in the possession of Brahmins
a cultivator who tills the land of others and gets half the crop as his share
powerful officials who developed landed interests
items.x: Ardhika (arthika) in early medieval texts is a sharecropper who tilled another's land for half the crop. A rent-free Brahmin village is an agrahara/brahmadeya.

items.s: During which age did women enjoy equality with men?
items.x: No period gave women equality with men; in the Gupta age their status fell (early marriage, no property rights), so 'None of these'.

items.s:
With reference to the temple of Bhitargaon, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, which of the following statements is/ are correct?
(1) This temple was constructed during 5th century A.D. to 6th century A.D.
(2) It is one of the oldest brick temples of India.
Select the correct answer using the code given below-
items.x: Both are correct: the Bhitargaon temple (Kanpur) is a Gupta brick temple of the 5th–6th century with terracotta panels, one of the oldest brick temples of India.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s:
As per the given table, match the avatars of Lord Vishnu in the sequence they are believed to appear as per Hindu beliefs.
Avatar:
(A) Matsya (The Fish)
(B) Kurma (The Tortoise)
(C) Varaha (The Boar)
(D) Narasimha (The Man-Lion)
Sequence: (i) First (ii) Second (iii) Third (iv) Fourth
items.x: The Dashavatara order begins Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha. Off-topic, moved.

items.s: The incarnation of Lord Vishnu in Dwapara Yuga was
items.x: Krishna is the avatar of the Dvapara Yuga (Dwarka is its dham); Rama belongs to the Treta Yuga, Vamana and Narasimha to earlier yugas.

items.s: Who has recited the 'Vishnusahasranama' for the first time?
items.x: In the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata, Bhishma recites the Vishnu Sahasranama to Yudhishthira.

items.s: The Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh is associated with which combination?
o: Vishnu, stone construction, shikhara and panchayatana plan
Brahmanical worship, brick construction and terracotta panels
Shiva, flat roof and scattered ruined remains
Parvati, two-storeyed roofed ambulatory and brick construction
items.x: The Deogarh Dashavatara Temple is a stone temple dedicated to Vishnu, with a shikhara and panchayatana plan. Its shikhara is now partly ruined.

items.s: Which of the following describes the Bhitargaon temple in Kanpur district?
o: Stone temple with a panchayatana plan
items.x: Bhitargaon is a Brahmanical brick temple of the 5th-6th century CE, noted for its terracotta panels.

items.s: Which Gupta temple has two flanking shrines at the entrance?
items.x: Bhumara has flanking shrines; Sanchi 17 a flat roof, Nachna a covered ambulatory and Deogarh a shikhara with panchayatana plan.

items.s: Which one of the following temples has a Dravida-style superstructure rather than a Nagara shikhara?
items.x: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal (like the Malegitti Shivalaya) is Dravida in style (UPSC 2026). The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh and the Huchimalligudi temple at Aihole have Nagara shikharas, and Bhitargaon has an early shikhara in the Nagara line.

items.s: Which Gupta temple has a covered ambulatory and is two-storeyed?
items.x: The Parvati temple at Nachna (Panna) is a stage-2 temple with a covered ambulatory and two storeys.

items.s: Which of the following temple – place pairs is correctly matched?
items.x: Tigawa is in Katni, MP. Dashavatara is at Deogarh (Lalitpur), Bhitargaon in Kanpur and the Nachna Parvati temple in Panna.

items.s: The stage-3 Gupta temple with a low square shikhara and panchayatana plan marks the start of which style?
items.x: Stage 3 (low shikhara, high jagati, panchayatana) marks the beginning of the northern Nagara style.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the stages of Gupta temple building:
1. Stage 1 temples had a square sanctum and a flat roof.
2. Stage 2 temples added a covered ambulatory.
3. Stage 3 temples had no shikhara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Stage 1 had a flat roof and stage 2 a covered ambulatory; stage 3 had a low square shikhara, so statement 3 is wrong.

items.s: Which Gupta temple, a flat-roofed single-cell stone shrine with a four-pillared porch, represents the first stage of Gupta temple building?
items.x: Temple 17 at Sanchi is a stage-1 temple: flat roof, single cell and a four-pillared porch.

items.s: Who founded the Pashupata sect?
items.x: The Pashupata sect of Shaivism traces its foundation to Lakulisha.

items.src: Indian History previous paper (header not legible)
items.s: The number 'zero' was first invented by whom?
items.x: Zero as a number with its own rules was developed in India (Brahmagupta, 628 AD; place-value notation). Off-topic (history of science), moved.

items.s: In whose rule Kalidasa lived?
items.x: Kalidasa is traditionally placed at the court of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (Gupta age); 'Vikramaditya' alone is the title, not a separate ruler here.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
items.s: Who was Aryabhata?
items.at: A well-known astronomer of ancient India
items.x: Aryabhata (5th century CE) was an astronomer-mathematician of ancient India who wrote the Aryabhatiya and explained Earth's rotation; India's first satellite (1975) was named after him.

items.s: The poet Bana was patronised by which of the following rulers?
items.x: Banabhatta, author of Harshacharita and Kadambari, was the court poet of Harsha – not of Chandragupta Maurya, Ashoka or Vikramaditya.

items.s: Nalanda University was destroyed by –
items.x: Nalanda was sacked by the army of the Turkish (Muslim) general Bakhtiyar Khalji at the end of the 12th century. The Kushans and Scythians were far earlier and the Mughals far later.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: Which of the following sites have been introduced in UNESCO's heritage list in 2016?
items.x: Nalanda Mahavihara (Bihar) was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in July 2016. Jantar Mantar Jaipur was listed in 2010, the Goa churches in 1986 and Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus in 2004.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
items.s:
Assertion (A): The Western Chalukyas claimed Brahmana origin as Haritiputras of the Manavya gotra and built a strong fortress at Vatapi.
Reason (R): Pulakeshin I established the independent power of the Western Chalukya dynasty in the 6th century CE.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct, but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect, but R is correct.
items.x: Both A and R are true: the Chalukyas called themselves Haritiputras of the Manavya gotra and Pulakesin I fortified Vatapi (Badami rock inscription, 543); R (founding independent power) is true but does not explain the claim of origin in A.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: The credit for construction of not only temples but also the carving styles of sculpture goes to which of the below mentioned dynasties?
items.x: The Pallavas pioneered structural and rock-cut temples (Mahabalipuram rathas, Shore Temple, Kailasanatha) and a distinct style of carved sculpture (Arjuna's Penance).

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Kokili belongs to which dynasty?
items.x: Kokkili (Kokkili Vikramaditya, 8th c.) was an Eastern Chalukya king of Vengi who briefly succeeded Vishnuvardhana III and was overthrown. He was not a Pallava, Ganga or Chola ruler.
